about: DadBox enclosure layout. Single source for hardware/cad/layout.py (checks, 1:1 drill templates) and enclosure-layout.html. Units mm. Interior frame: x from the inner LEFT wall (as the child faces the front), y from the inner FRONT wall, z up from the tub floor; the lid's inner face is at z = H. The tub stands the right way up: its floor is the BOTTOM, the flat lid is the TOP FACE (ADR 0023 as revised 2026-09-29). Anchors: ax left|right says which wall x is measured from (to the part's near edge, or to a cylinder's centre); ay front|back likewise for y. z values may be expressions in H.

box.outer_source: Temu listing 188 x 120 x 37 mm / order 188 x 119 x 37.5 mm
box.inner_note: Planning values, not measured: wall ~3 mm at the rim plus ~1 mm draft toward the tub floor, tub floor ~3 mm, lid ~3 mm. Replace with calipers.

bosses.note: Lid-screw columns, full height, threaded at the rim. Six on this clone: the lid has four corner holes and two mid-way along the long walls (photo 2026-09-29).

parts.label: Modem HAT
parts.fix: 4 x M2.5 nylon standoffs, 5 mm, on the tub floor with M2.5 x 6 pan-head screws from below (hidden under the box, beside the rubber feet). Mark the holes through the board itself. USB-A ports toward the front wall, Pi's ports toward the speaker.

parts.label: Pi Zero 2 W
parts.fix: On the HAT's own brass standoffs, as delivered. Its micro-USB ports face the speaker: use an angled micro-USB plug for PWR IN if a straight one hits.

parts.label: Soldered leads
parts.fix: Wires soldered straight into the Pi's GPIO holes, bent flat, tied to an adhesive mount. A straight header with dupont plugs stands ~22 mm above the Pi and would hit the lid.

parts.label: Amp
parts.fix: 2 mm double-sided foam tape (VHB) on insulating film on the tub floor; trim the pins flush underneath first. One cable tie over its leads to an adhesive mount.

parts.label: Foam block
parts.fix: Closed-cell foam cut to fill the gap under the speaker, glued to the tub floor. It presses the speaker up against the lid when the lid is screwed on.

parts.label: Speaker
parts.fix: Cone facing up under the grille. The foam ring with the round hole sits between cone face and lid: it is the seal. The foam block below presses it up; no screws through the lid.

parts.label: Record

hole.drill: step drill 15, then round file to 16

parts.fix: Its own nut from inside the lid, gasket outside under the flange, a drop of medium threadlocker. Keep 26 mm clear below it for the body, solder tabs and leads.

hole.drill: step drill 15, then round file to 16

parts.label: Mic
parts.fix: Sound hole centred on a 2 mm hole in the lid, sealed with a ring punched from foam tape; the foam column below presses it up (as in the mock-up), a bead of hot glue holds it to the lid while you assemble. Never records while the speaker plays, so beside it is fine.

parts.label: Antenna
parts.fix: Nut and lock washer, medium threadlocker. Its body grounds the aluminium to the modem. The hinged stub folds upright. The U.FL end clips onto the HAT's LTE connector.

parts.label: 5 V in

hole.drill: 22.3 mm for the EX-49222 (it takes 22.3 to 24) - step drill

parts.fix: Its own nut. Its 30 cm tail (USB-C plug) runs along the back wall behind the speaker into a USB-C-socket-to-micro-USB adapter at the Pi's PWR IN; coil the slack under the speaker. Not a socket-to-socket coupler: a plug has one CC wire, a coupler two, so the supply comes on one way up only.

battery.label: UPS Module 3S (deferred)
battery.note: Height is an estimate: 18650 cells in holders on a board. Shown only to test whether it could be added later.
